{{Short description|German mathematician}}
[[File: Wilhelm Winter, 2012.jpg | thumb|Wilhelm Winter, 2012.]]
'''Wilhelm Winter''' (born 1968) is a German [[mathematician]], specializing in [[operator algebra]]s (and particularly [[C*-algebra]]s).

==Education and career==
Winter received in 1996 his [[Diplom]] from the [[Heidelberg University]] and in 2000 his doctorate ([[Promotion (Germany)|Promotion]]) from the [[University of Münster]] with thesis advisor [[Joachim Cuntz]] and thesis ''Covering Dimension for Nuclear C*-Algebras''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=45469}}</ref> At the University of Münster he was a research assistant from 2001 to 2007 and habilitated there in 2006 in Münster. In Fall 2002 he was a visiting assistant professor at [[Texas A & M University]]. From 2007 to 2011 he was at [[University of Nottingham]], first as a lecturer and later as a reader. Winter is a professor of mathematics at the University of Münster since 2011.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wilhelm Winter, C.V.|website=University of Münster|url=https://ivv5hpp.uni-muenster.de/u/wwinter/wwinter/cv.html}}</ref>

In 2010 he received with [[Andrew Toms]] the G. de B. Robinson Award.<ref>{{cite web|title=G. de B. Robinson Award|website=Canadian Mathematical Society|url=https://cms.math.ca/Prizes/info/gbr}}</ref> In 2018 Winter was an invited speaker  with talk ''Structure of nuclear C*-algebras: From quasidiagonality to classification, and back again'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Rio de Janeiro.<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Winter, Wilhelm|eprint=1712.00247|title=Structure of nuclear C*-algebras: From quasidiagonality to classification, and back again|year=2018|class=math.OA}}</ref>
